newsitem.title: CHINA: Daughter-in-law says China's Mao gave HK schedule.
newsitem.headline: Daughter-in-law says China's Mao gave HK schedule.

text.p: A daughter-in-law of China's late Chairman Mao Zedong said on Thursday that the founder of communist China had forecast a schedule for the handover of Hong Kong as early as 1974, well before Deng Xiaoping sealed the deal.
"I could say that more than 20 years ago, Chairman Mao...had arranged a schedule for the return of Hong Kong," Shao Hua, wife of Mao's younger son, Mao Anqing, told China Central Television.

Hong Kong returned to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on Monday after 156 years of British colonial rule and on the expiry of a 99-year lease under which London took control of the New Territories district of the territory.
Beijing credits Deng for regaining Hong Kong under a 1984 treaty with Britain.
Mao's daughter-in-law said his role in what Beijing has hailed as one of the events of the year should not be forgotten.
"In 1959, Chairman Mao had said that it was better temporarily not to take Hong Kong back," said Shao, wife of Mao's only surviving son. His elder son Mao Anying was killed in the 1950-53 Korean War.

"In 1974, when receiving the British Prime Minister (Edward Heath), Chairman Mao told him that in 1997 there should be a peaceful handover of Hong Kong," she said. "What would be done at that time would be negotiated."
Mao died in 1976 and Deng took power two years later, returning from the political wilderness after Mao purged him in 1971 and again in 1975.
